try:
            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as handle:
                handle.write(self.token)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
evidence.reason: The Hold protocol's own comments and error contract claim crash-persistent admission: after O_CREAT|O_EXCL the marker 'exists even if the token never lands' (line 406) and must keep holding admission until its bytes are verified (lines 414-426). But acquire() only fsyncs the token file (line 412); it never fsyncs self.path.parent, so the new directory entry can be lost on power failure after the file sync, rebooting the host with no admission hold despite the code's stated guarantee, and symmetrically the release unlink at line 459 is not made durable, so a stale hold can reappear. This is an implementation error in the existing admission-hold durability behavior, not a request for new scope; the repair is local (fsync the parent after creation/removal and surface failure as the same unverified-recovery outcome already used for fsync failure) and requires no owner decision because it does not change the admission semantics or interface, only makes the already-promised persistence real.
